why.text: Clay and limy foothill soils mostly below 300 m, on ventilated east-southeast slopes with a moderate summer water deficit, planted mainly to Grechetto gentile.

styles.text: White wines, still (superiore, Classico) or lightly sparkling (frizzante) and fully sparkling (spumante).

climate.text: Rain averages 800 mm on the high plain to 1,200 mm in the highest hills. Mean temperatures run 14 to 12 °C, falling with height. Low hills have a moderate water deficit of up to 350 mm a year.

soil.text: Fine-textured clay soils on Argille Scagliose and Blue Clays, plus silty, very calcareous soils. Sandstone ridges and Yellow Sands also occur.

altitude.text: Vines grow mostly below 300 m. Above about 400 m it is wetter and cooler.

tastes.text: Straw yellow, with white flowers and pear and apple, ripe in the still wines and less ripe in the sparkling. Dry to off-dry, with almond and citrus notes, sometimes slightly bitter.

styles.name: Classico Superiore
styles.text: Still wine, at least 95% Grechetto gentile, from the oldest zone, 12% alcohol minimum.

styles.name: Superiore
styles.text: Still wine, at least 85% Grechetto gentile, 11.5% alcohol minimum, dry to off-dry.

styles.name: Frizzante
styles.text: Lightly sparkling, dry; bottle-fermented versions must say 'rifermentazione in bottiglia'.

styles.name: Spumante
styles.text: Sparkling, from brut nature to extra dry, 11% alcohol minimum.

why.text: Albana grown on clay and limestone hills around the Spungone ridge, in sunny south-facing vineyards, gives apricot-scented wines of many styles.

others: Other white grapes suitable for Emilia-Romagna (up to 5%)

styles.text: White Albana in five types: secco, amabile, dolce, passito and passito riserva.

climate.text: The spec gives no figures; it says Albana does best with good sun exposure and brightness.

soil.text: Clay or silty clay with varying limestone, and yellow sands low in limestone. Best around the Spungone, a Pliocene sandy limestone ridge set in clays.

altitude.text: Excellent results above 100 m above sea level, mostly in south-east to south-west facing vineyards.

tastes.text: Secco: straw yellow, dry, slightly tannic, warm and harmonious. Amabile and dolce: fruity, straw turning golden with age. Passito: intense, golden to amber. A sage-like note, apricot tending to lead.

styles.name: Secco
styles.text: Dry white, at least 12% alcohol and 4.5 g/l acidity.

styles.name: Passito
styles.text: Sweet wine from dried grapes, at least 17% alcohol, 70 g/l sugar.

styles.name: Passito riserva
styles.text: Sweet, from dried or noble-rot grapes, at least 24% total alcohol.

styles.name: Amabile
styles.text: Fruity off-dry white, at least 12.5% total alcohol.
